comments.text:
I've maintained, as have many of my Māori whanau/iwi (people) maintained since forever, that Māori cuisine is the only cuisine authentic to Aotearoa. But typical to near all of Pākeha, as this beautiful Pākeha states at 4:50sec, Pākeha only hear what Māori have been trying to teach ignorant Pākeha, when it comes from another Pākeha. 
In short, all of what's detailed in this video re the kaitiakitanga of our kai, is steeped in Matauaranga Māori. That is, Māori cosmology and our celestial realm. Of which the Pākeha equivalent, is worded as, science. 
What this man presents, is how many of our Marae still operate. This kai on display here being sold for 100's of 1000's of dollar$$, is how we eat on our Marae, all the time. That's right. What ypu all are oo-ing and aah-ing over, is normal for us Māori. 
So tēnā koe to the author of this video. And respect to this good Pākeha chef too. Especially for not being so arrogant to not to forget to acknowledge the source of his knowledge base, Māori, and Ozzy! (Kia Glen bro!)
Na reira, you Pākeha that constantly belittle Māori and move toward trying to disenfranchise Māori in our own country that you try to reduce us to being 2nd class citizens, the beauty this chef displays in his appreciation for just one-single-taonga derived from my Te Ao Māori,  is only a portion of what you could otherwise have if ypu chose to embrace the only culture that is authentic to Aotearoa, Māori, instead of constantly hating us. End of day, it makes no real difference to us, as what ypu think and say about Māori, is a measure of you and your own ignorance and insecurity. 
And for the record, to all whom think that we Māori are "kiwis", we're not. Kiwi is an identity to he had by those whom want to authenticate themselves to Aotearoa. We Māori dont suffer that identity crisis. Because we already ARE authenticated. Because we - belong here! And "kiwi" is a Māori word that Pākeha prefer to use because they don't like my other word for them, Pākeha 🙄🤥🫩. Yeah, go figure ..
Kia ora koutou.
